title: chromatographR: An introduction to HPLC-DAD analysis
text: chromatographR package reproducible analysis HPLC-DAD data R. Liquid chromatography coupled diode-array detection (HPLC-DAD) remains one popular analytical methodologies due convenience low-cost. However, currently open-source tools available analyzing HPLC-DAD chromatograms “simple” chromatographic data. use proprietary software analysis HPLC-DAD data currently significant barrier reproducible science, since tools widely accessible, usually require users select complicated options graphical user interface easily repeated. Reproducibility much higher command line workflows, like chromatographR, entire analysis can stored easily repeated anyone using publicly available software. chromatographR package began fork previously published alsace package (Wehrens et al. 2015), reworked improved functions peak-finding, integration peak table generation well number new tools data visualization downstream analysis. Unlike alsace, emphasized multivariate curve resolution alternating least squares (MCR-ALS), chromatographR developed around conventional workflow seem familiar users standard software tools HPLC-DAD analysis. chromatographR includes tools ) pre-processing, b) retention-time alignment, c) peak-finding, d) peak-integration e) peak-table construction, well additional functions useful analyzing resulting peak table.

title: chromatographR: An introduction to HPLC-DAD analysis
text: Variable penalty dynamic time warping another algorithm can effective correcting retention time shifts (Clifford et al. 2009; Clifford Stone 2012). Instead calculating explicit warping function, dynamic time warping (DTW) works repeatedly shifting, expanding contracting time axis small steps satisfactory alignment attained. process can result close matching peaks, can also lead severe peak distortion time axis repeatedly expanded /contracted (Tomasi et al. 2004). Variable penalty dynamic time warping derivative DTW constrains expansion contraction time-axis applying penalty types “risky” moves. can often achieve good alignment minimal peak distortion. VPdtw package suggested dependency since requires working C++ compiler. Unlike PTW, VPdtw can take single wavelength input (returns global warping whole chromatographic matrix). code snippet uses VPdtw warp example chromatograms using first chromatogram reference. penalty maxshift parameters can adjusted control degree warping. Comparison variable penalty dynamic time warping (VPdtw) aligned chromatograms (top) raw data (bottom). Chromatograms can also visualized heatmaps plot_chroms_heatmap, can powerful way check alignment chromatograms across samples. Comparison variable penalty dynamic time warping (VPdtw) aligned chromatograms (top) raw data (bottom) via heatmap plot. case alignments produced two algorithms quite similar, cases one algorithm may dramatically outperform . experience, alignments generated VPdtw less prone overfitting. However, PTW algorithm interpretable since fits explicit model data. Examination coefficients models can often useful identification problematic samples.

Alternative options include "mean", "median", "max", last uses intense peak cluster directly rather aggregating. reproduce previous behavior, set summarize_by = "mean". Added automatic thinning chromatograms plot_chroms speed plotting raw data. time resolution can adjusted new time_resolution argument. Changed behavior plot_chroms legend longer displayed default avoid overloading plots many chromatograms. export_spectrum == TRUE always return spectra invisibly plot_spectrum plot_all_spectra avoid cluttering console. Corrected get_peaks return model-fitted peak heights rather raw peak heights. changes numerical output workflows relied previous (incorrect) behavior. Removed index chr arguments across plotting functions, previously deprecated v0.7.0. Use idx instead. Deprecated arguments get_peaks still using dot notation (e.g., sd.max).
